# US-002 — Build a typed project graph from .planr/ with delegate-or-fallback sourcing

**Story ID:** US-002  
**Priority:** P1  
**Tasks:** T-002  
**Status:** Shipped (QA PASS)

## Who uses this and why

This story is the data backbone of every view in the dashboard. A planr user
never interacts with this layer directly — they see its output in the Overview
KPIs, the Graph DAG, the Board columns, and the Detail inspector. The goal is to
ensure that whatever the dashboard shows is always consistent with what
`/planr-pipeline:status` would report for the same project, so two tools never
disagree.

## What it does

The graph data engine (`lib/dashboard/graph-engine.mjs`) orchestrates two paths:

**A.1 — CLI delegate.** If the planr CLI is installed and at version >= 1.7.2,
the engine shells out to `planr graph --json` (preferred) or `planr status --json`
as a fallback. The JSON output is coerced to the `{ nodes, edges }` shape,
validated against `schemas/v1.0.0/graph.schema.json`, and returned.

**A.2 — Native frontmatter reader.** When the CLI is absent or outdated, the
native reader (`lib/dashboard/graph-reader.mjs`) takes over. It recursively walks
`.planr/`, parses each artifact's YAML frontmatter with a minimal stdlib-only
parser (no npm dependencies), infers the node type from the file path and id
prefix, classifies the status using the same rules as `/status` A.2, and
constructs hierarchy edges (`contains`) and dependency edges (`depends_on`). The
result is validated against the same schema before returning.

Both paths produce identical `{ nodes, edges }` shapes. A conformance test
(`tests/dashboard/graph-equivalence.test.mjs`) asserts that the two paths produce
equivalent node sets on the shared fixture project
(`conformance/fixtures/dashboard-graph/`).

## The Graph schema

`schemas/v1.0.0/graph.schema.json` is a JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 document that
defines:

- **Node types:** `epic | feature | story | task | spec | backlog | quick | sprint | adr` (9 values)
- **Status values:** `done | in-progress | blocked | outstanding | addressed` (5 values)
- **Edge kinds:** `contains` (hierarchy from frontmatter parent ids) | `depends_on` (from `dependsOn` arrays)
- **Optional node fields:** `githubIssue`, `linearIssueIdentifier`, `body` (detail view only)

The schema is `additionalProperties: false` on both node and edge shapes, so any
field the reader emits must be declared here.

## Status classification

`classifyStatus(rawStatus)` in `graph-reader.mjs` maps raw frontmatter status
values to the five enum values:

| Raw value | Classified as |
|-----------|---------------|
| done, closed, completed, shipped, released | `done` |
| promoted, superseded | `addressed` |
| blocked | `blocked` |
| in-progress, in_progress, in progress | `in-progress` |
| anything else | `outstanding` |

## Type inference

`inferType(relDir, id)` determines the node type from the file's path relative to
`.planr/`. Directory takes precedence (e.g. a file in `.planr/epics/` is always
`epic`). The `id` prefix is a fallback when the directory is not one of the
recognized top-level names. Inside `.planr/specs/SPEC-NNN-*/`, files in a
`stories/` subdirectory are `story`, files in `tasks/` are `task`, and the spec
root file is `spec`.

## Known limitation

See the **Drift findings** section in [`api.md`](./api.md#known-limitation-native-reader-surfaces-loose-planrmd-files-as-nodes).
The native reader walks all `.md` files under `.planr/` without a directory
allowlist, so loose files (e.g. `.planr/ESTIMATION.md`,
`.planr/checklists/AGILE-DEVELOPMENT-GUIDE.md`) and `qa-report.md` files inside
spec directories are ingested as nodes. The CLI delegate path does not have this
issue. This means the two paths can diverge on a real project even though they
agree on the controlled conformance fixture.

## Acceptance criteria (all passing)

- The graph module produces a `Graph` object validated against `schemas/v1.0.0/graph.schema.json`.
- Node types match the 9-value enum; edge kinds match the 2-value enum.
- Status is classified using the same rules as `/planr-pipeline:status` A.2.
- When CLI >= v1.7.2 is available, the engine delegates to it.
- When the CLI is absent, the native reader produces an equivalent, schema-valid graph.
- `tests/dashboard/graph-equivalence.test.mjs` passes (3/3 subtests).
- `githubIssue` and `linearIssueIdentifier` are hoisted to the node level when present in frontmatter.
- An empty `.planr/` produces `{ nodes: [], edges: [] }` without throwing.
